name: PyramidKV (layer-dependent KV budget) - NOT KV quantization
bits: none - allocates different KV cache SIZES per layer (more in lower layers, less in higher ones) rather than reducing bits.
activation_scheme: None. Based on Pyramidal Information Funneling: attention scatters widely in lower layers, consolidates in middle layers, and concentrates on a few critical tokens in higher layers. The KV budget is therefore allocated inversely - more cache low, less cache high - diverging from uniform-budget methods.
kernels: Evaluated on LongBench and Needle-in-a-Haystack; no specific kernel named in the abstract.
quality_delta: From the abstract: matches full-KV-cache performance on LongBench while retaining only 12% of the KV cache; at an extreme 0.7% retention it surpasses other KV compression techniques with up to 20.5 absolute accuracy improvement on TREC; retaining just 128 KV entries gives LLaMA-3-70B 100.0 accuracy on Needle-in-a-Haystack.
notes: GROUP SIZE NOT APPLICABLE BY CONSTRUCTION: eviction reduces HOW MANY KV positions are retained; no bits per retained value change, so there is no weight grid to group. The null here is a fact about the method, not missing data. Boundary record, and the most surprising one: 128 total KV entries is a compression ratio so extreme that it stops being about compression and becomes about caching only attention sinks. That is a real finding about where attention information actually lives, and it is worth reading alongside KIVI - if a handful of entries carry most of the attention mass, then spending 4 bits per entry on the rest is largely wasted. Boundary stated plainly because the 12%-of-KV-cache phrasing sounds like a bit-width claim and is not one.
